subject.title: [Bug]: Session transcript mirroring writes header cwd from process.cwd(), allowing cross-agent workspace contamination

question: Should maintainers adopt/rebase the linked transcript-header cwd fix, replace it with a fresh narrow PR, or close that PR and keep this issue for a different implementation?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and security/session-state sensitive, but an open conflicting closing PR already owns the narrow fix path, so automation should not queue a parallel fix without maintainer direction.

options.title: Adopt or rebase the linked fix
options.body: Refresh the open fix PR or replace it with an equivalent current-main patch that removes the ambient cwd fallback for mirrored transcript headers.

options.title: Keep issue open and close the stale PR
options.body: Close the conflicting contributor branch if maintainers do not want to revive it, but keep this issue as the canonical bug until a new fix lands.

options.title: Defer for broader cwd cleanup
options.body: Leave both paths paused if maintainers want this solved only as part of a wider process.chdir isolation refactor.

recommendation.title: Adopt or rebase the linked fix
recommendation.body: Refresh the open fix PR or replace it with an equivalent current-main patch that removes the ambient cwd fallback for mirrored transcript headers.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the delivery mirror behavior and is the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether to adopt or replace the linked fix.
